items.title: Continuum generalized entropy beyond the regulated model
items.design_state: A conditional research question for an existing four-dimensional semiclassical Einstein-scalar collapse solution; asks for finite regulator-independent generalized-entropy differences and future monotonicity without assuming modular-energy/area balance.
items.physical_scope: A precisely delimited open problem for a selected four-dimensional semiclassical Einstein-scalar collapse model, an actually existing smooth solution on a stated globally hyperbolic domain, a Hadamard state, and a fixed covariant renormalization prescription. It asks for sufficient nonperturbative-in-the-scalar-amplitude conditions for finite, regulator-independent generalized-entropy differences and their future monotonicity. It asserts no solution existence, entropy convergence, regulator independence, generalized second law, or empirical result.
items.statement: Determine checkable sufficient conditions on a specified semiclassical Einstein-scalar collapse model, an existing smooth solution, a Hadamard state, ordered smooth horizon cuts, and a nonempty class of admissible ultraviolet regulator sequences that yield finite regulator-independent generalized-entropy differences with nonnegative future ordering, without a scalar-amplitude truncation or an assumed modular-energy/area balance identity.

title: Precisely isolated horizon research questions — Examples

items.title: Research labels confer no theorem premises
items.design_state: A bounded source-status remark distinguishing the adopted effective equation, conditional horizon-algebra results, perturbative apparent-horizon results, and replica/ensemble calculations; it makes no universal-theorem or unitarity claim.
items.physical_scope: A bounded, source-based statement of inference limits for selected semiclassical-collapse, horizon-algebra, apparent-horizon, island, and JT results reviewed through 22 October 2026. It records their model assumptions and the exact non-claims of the adopted semiclassical equation. It does not prove nonexistence of a result elsewhere, falsify a universal claim, establish a measured fact, or imply microscopic unitarity.
items.statement: The adopted semiclassical equation is an effective model and does not assert solution existence, uniqueness, or stability. Kirklin's exact modified GSL is for idealized dynamical quantum-reference-frame cuts and retains a later-cut free-energy term; its ordinary-GSL limit is approximate and conditional. The other cited GSL, apparent-horizon, island, and JT results retain their stated model assumptions and do not by themselves establish the local fixed-scheme regulator-independent limit in the open problem or generic evaporation unitarity.
